sources_add.title: Witness Statement of Benjamin Steinmetz, 2 September 2015 (BSG Resources Limited v Republic of Guinea, ICSID Case No. ARB/14/22)
sources_add.publisher: International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes

beny-steinmetz.note: Blanked by fact-check. I opened the witness statement on icsid.worldbank.org and confirmed every figure is in it: para 3 (2003 consolidation into BSGR), para 4 ('The BSG group now operates in more than 20 countries worldwide'), para 12 (BSGR 'has had operations in 14 countries' and 'has employed over 8,000 people'), para 14 ('more than 120 prospective deals on four continents over the last decade'). The figures are accurately reported, but they cannot carry a 'what he oversaw' sentence: (1) they are his own untested assertions in a pleading he filed to win money from Guinea in the ICSID arbitration, with no audited or third-party corroboration - BSGR publishes no annual report; (2) the 14-country and 8,000-employee claims carry no year and are in the present perfect ('has had', 'has employed'), so they cannot be tied to any period, let alone to the years of the Simandou case; (3) in the same document, paras 1, 15 and 16, he states he is not a director of any company and not a shareholder, and is paid a flat advisory fee - so the brief's question, how much he oversaw in a post, has no post to attach to here. Rule from the brief that decides it: 'Pick the post through which they acted in the map's cases... If the person acted alone or in one post with no countable output, write "".'

bill-turner.total: As Anvil Mining's president and chief executive from 8 January 2004, he ran a company with three producing mines, Dikulushi, Kulu and Kinsevere, all in the Democratic Republic of Congo, exploration interests in the DRC, Zambia and the Philippines, and 4,390 people at its operations as of 29 February 2008, 2,750 of them direct employees (Anvil Mining Limited, Annual Information Form for the year ended 31 December 2007).

sources_add.title: Anvil Mining Limited, Annual Information Form for the financial year ended 31 December 2007 (dated 28 March 2008)
sources_add.publisher: Anvil Mining Limited, filed with the Australian Securities Exchange

bill-turner.note: Confirmed unchanged. I opened the ASX Annual Information Form in two passes (characters 0-100,000 and 100,000-200,000) on announcements.asx.com.au. Verified in the document: Turner is President and CEO and a director of Anvil Mining Limited from 8 January 2004; managing director of Anvil Mining NL July 2003 to 8 January 2004; general manager July 1995 to July 2003; director of Anvil Mining NL since 23 September 1996 - so the company-scale figures fall inside his tenure. Verified the three producing mines in the DRC (Dikulushi in commercial production since October 2002, Kulu producing, Kinsevere ramping up from December 2006), exploration interests in the DRC, Zambia and the Philippines, and 'As of February 29, 2008, the AVM Group employs 4,390 people, of whom 2,750 are direct employees'. One internal inconsistency in the source, not in the sentence: the per-site direct-employee figures (Dikulushi 1,020, Kulu 340, Kinsevere 850, other 360) sum to 2,570, not the 2,750 the document states; the sentence uses the document's own stated total, which is the right call, and the per-site breakdown is not in the sentence. The headcount is February 2008, four years into his tenure and over three years after the October 2004 Kilwa killings; the sentence dates it explicitly, so it does not pass off a 2008 figure as a 2004 one.

ira-rennert.total: He is chairman and chief executive of The Renco Group, which through trusts he established controls The Doe Run Resources Corporation; in the year to 31 October 2001 Doe Run held eight production shafts along Missouri's Viburnum Trend, six of them operating and two on care and maintenance, plus the La Oroya smelter and the Cobriza mine in Peru, and employed 400 salaried and 1,138 hourly staff in the United States and 955 salaried, 2,131 hourly and 1,475 contract workers in Peru, with net sales of $303.1 million in the United States and $434.3 million in Peru (Doe Run Resources Corporation, Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 31 October 2001, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission).

sources_add.title: The Doe Run Resources Corporation, Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 31 October 2001

ira-rennert.note: Corrected. One factual change: the writer's sentence said Doe Run 'ran eight production shafts'. The 10-K says the Missouri operations have eight production shafts along about 40 miles of the Viburnum Trend, of which six are currently operating, with Viburnum-29 and West Fork on care and maintenance (Item 1 refers to 'six production shafts'). 'Ran eight' overstates it, so the sentence now says eight shafts, six operating and two on care and maintenance. Everything else verified in the filing: Rennert is Renco's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Renco is owned by trusts he established for himself and members of his family; 'Mr. Rennert controls the Company and its subsidiaries'; La Oroya bought from Centromin on 23 October 1997 and Cobriza acquired August 1998; employees as of 31 October 2001 - US 400 active salaried and 1,138 active hourly, Peru 955 active salaried, 2,131 active hourly and 1,475 contractors; net sales US $303.1m, Peru $434.3m (consolidated $737.5m after eliminations). The sentence correctly presents these as Doe Run's figures, not Renco Group's. Fetch note: the URL in the input (edgar/data/1061112/...) was refused by WebFetch with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED - a lapsed fetch permission, the request was never put to the user - and a direct curl to www.sec.gov returned HTTP 403 'Your Request Originates from an Undeclared Automated Tool', a server refusal. I did not spoof a user agent. I located the same filing through one web search, which yielded the equivalent zero-padded path (edgar/data/0001061112/...), and WebFetch opened that successfully; the source URL above is updated to the one that opens. renco-group.com remains unreadable (robots_disallowed), so there is still no group-wide Renco figure.

iskandar-safa.total: As Privinvest's chairman, a post the English High Court found was 'executive, and full-time executive' and in which 'no major activity proceeded without his knowledge and approval, including of the figures', he approved the group's three supply contracts with Mozambican state companies, signed between January 2013 and May 2014 for maritime surveillance, a tuna fleet and a shipyard, worth, after change orders and increases, a total approaching US$2 billion, more than 12 per cent of Mozambique's GDP (High Court of Justice, Business and Property Courts, Republic of Mozambique v Credit Suisse International and others, judgment of 29 July 2024).

sources_add.title: Republic of Mozambique v Credit Suisse International and others, judgment (29 July 2024)
sources_add.publisher: High Court of Justice of England and Wales, Business and Property Courts (Commercial Court)

iskandar-safa.note: Corrected. One factual change: the writer's sentence said Safa 'signed three supply contracts in 2013 and 2014'. I read the judgment in two passes (characters 0-100,000 and 100,000-200,000) and it nowhere records him signing any of the three. The signatories it names are: Proindicus, 18 January 2013, with Privinvest Shipbuilding SAL; EMATUM, 2 August 2013, with Abu Dhabi Mar LLC, signed by Mr Allam as CFO and by Mr do Rosario and another for EMATUM; MAM, 1 May 2014, with Privinvest Shipbuilding Investments LLC, signed by Mr Boustani for Privinvest and Mr do Rosario for MAM. Safa appears as a 33 per cent owner of Privinvest, not as a signatory. The sentence now says he approved them, which is what the court actually found, and gives the contract window as the dates the judgment supplies. Verified unchanged: para 26, his chairmanship was 'executive, and full-time executive'; para 29, 'I am satisfied no major activity proceeded without his knowledge and approval, including of the figures'; para 7, 'after change orders and increases, a total of approaching US$2 billion' and 'more than 12% of GDP'. Para 30 records his own evidence that he was 'the final decision-maker to say whether I approve the transaction' but not the contract's content, which the corrected wording fits. Two further things in the judgment that the sentence does not need but the owner should know: at para 23 the judge did not accept Safa as a consistently truthful witness, and at para 34(b) the judgment states only what the outcome on the Safa claims would have been, because he died before judgment. No group-wide count of shipyards, employees or countries survives: the undated CEO Magazine '2,000 vessels' claim stays out, and privinvest.com could not be opened (permission request unanswered).

joseph-stiglitz.figure_for_owner: World Bank fiscal 1998 and fiscal 1999 (1 July 1997 to 30 June 1999): the Bank's executive directors approved 229 IBRD/IDA lending operations in fiscal 1998 (105 IBRD loans, 124 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1998, Appendix 14) and 276 in fiscal 1999 (131 IBRD loans, 145 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1999, Appendix 14) - 505 over the two years, which is this map's sum of the two reports. What that counts: IBRD loans and IDA credits approved by the Board. Both appendices state that supplements are included in the amounts but are not counted as separate lending operations, and that joint IBRD/IDA operations are counted once, as IBRD operations. It excludes IFC and MIGA entirely, and excludes GEF, Montreal Protocol, guarantees, recipient-executed trust-fund activities, carbon offset, special financing and debt-reduction operations. Why these two years: the officer lists in the annual reports, dated 30 June 1997, 30 June 1998 and 30 June 1999, each name 'Joseph E. Stiglitz, Senior Vice President, Development Economics, and Chief Economist', and his Nobel autobiography says 'I left the World Bank in January 2000', so fiscal 1998 and 1999 are the two full fiscal years wholly inside the period he is recorded in the post; fiscal 1997 and fiscal 2000 are each only partly covered and are not in the 505. For comparison, the World Bank projects API over the same dates returns 597 operations by board approval date, made up of 544 IBRD/IDA, 19 GEF Medium Sized Program, 13 Global Environment Project, 9 Recipient Executed Activities, 4 Debt Reduction Facility, 4 Guarantees, 3 Rainforest and 1 Montreal Protocol, of which 25 rows are supplements or additional financings counted separately - so the API figure is not a lending total and is not comparable with the annual reports' 505.

joseph-stiglitz.note: Total left blank, as instructed; no total written. figure_for_owner checked line by line and left unchanged - every number in it is on a page I opened. The PDF URLs in the input were refused by WebFetch with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (lapsed fetch permission, the request was never put to the user), so I downloaded the World Bank's own OCR text versions of the same documents from documents1.worldbank.org by curl and read them directly. Confirmed: Annual Report 1998, Appendix 14, 'Grand total 105 17,282.0 124 7,060.4 229 24,342.4' - 105 IBRD loans, 124 IDA credits, 229 operations. Annual Report 1999, Appendix 14, 'Bankwide total 131 22,182.3 145 6,811.8 276 28,994.1' - 131, 145, 276. 229 + 276 = 505; the text says plainly that this is this map's sum of the two reports. Both appendices carry the footnote 'Supplements are included in the amount but are not counted as separate lending operations. Joint IBRD/IDA operations are counted only once, as IBRD operations', as the text states. Officer lists confirmed, each headed with its date: 'OFFICERS OF THE WORLD BANK ... June 30, 1997', '... June 30, 1998', '... June 30, 1999', each naming 'Senior Vice President, Development Economics, and Chief Economist  Joseph E. Stiglitz'. The Nobel biographical page confirms the sentence 'I left the World Bank in January 2000'. The API comparison also checks out: the projects API returns total 597 for 1 July 1997 to 30 June 1999, exactly as stated, and the text is right to say it is not a lending total and not comparable. One small thing the owner may want added, not an error: the 1999 appendix carries a further footnote, 'Excludes an IDA HIPC grant of $150 million to Mozambique'. That is an exclusion from the amounts, not from the count of 276, so it does not change the 505. The field states plainly what it counts, what it excludes, why those two fiscal years and that the 505 is a sum made here. Whether to use it is the owner's call and I take no view.

lawrence-summers.figure_for_owner: World Bank fiscal 1991 and fiscal 1992 (1 July 1990 to 30 June 1992): the Bank's executive directors approved 229 IBRD/IDA lending operations in fiscal 1991 (126 IBRD loans, 103 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1991, Table 7-1) and 222 in fiscal 1992 (112 IBRD loans, 110 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1992, Table 7-1) - 451 over the two years, which is this map's sum of the two reports. What that counts: IBRD loans and IDA credits approved by the Board. Both tables state that supplements are included in the amounts but are not counted as separate lending operations, and that joint IBRD/IDA operations are counted once, as IBRD operations. It excludes IFC and MIGA entirely, and excludes GEF, Montreal Protocol, guarantees, trust-fund activities and debt-reduction operations. Why these two years: the officer lists in the annual reports, dated 30 June 1991 and 30 June 1992, both name 'Lawrence H. Summers, Vice President, Development Economics and Chief Economist', while the list in the 1993 report names 'D.C. Rao (Acting)' in the post, so fiscal 1991 and 1992 are the two full fiscal years in which he is recorded in it; the part of fiscal 1993 he served is not in the 451. For comparison, the World Bank projects API over the same dates returns 309 operations by board approval date, made up of 304 IBRD/IDA, 2 Global Environment Project, 2 Debt Reduction Facility and 1 Montreal Protocol, of which 24 rows are supplements or additional financings counted separately - far below the annual reports' 451 for the same window, so the API's early-1990s coverage appears incomplete and the API figure should not be used here.

sources_add.title: Lenir Perez, presidente del Grupo EMCO Holding: un visionario que lidera importantes proyectos
sources_add.publisher: Revista Estrategia y Negocios (E&N BrandLab, commissioned by EMCO Holding)

lenir-perez.note: Blanked by fact-check. I opened the E&N page and the writer's description of it is accurate: it carries the label 'POR E&N PARA EMCO HOLDING', is dated 17 December 2021, names Lenir Perez Solis as president of Emco Holding Inc, and puts group assets above $700 million for 2021 (with sales projected above $1,000 million for 2022, Palmerola over $200 million, Tocoa $200 million, El Salvador cargo terminal phases of $13.3 million and $49 million, cold chain over $125,000, Puente Alto Energy about 4,000 million lempiras for 100 MW, and AeroMetro with no figure; Tocoa jobs 'over 800' now and 'over 3,000' once operating). It fails on three counts. First, independence: it is content commissioned by the subject's own company about the subject, so the $700 million is the group's own unaudited claim about itself, with no filing, auditor or registry behind it - the standard the brief sets is a sourced figure, and a disclosure inline does not convert a self-published number into a checked one. Second, shape: the brief asks how many projects, loans or deals the person oversaw; this is a dollar asset total, and the article gives no count of group companies, no group headcount and no project count. Third, the article mixes 2021 actuals with 2022 projections, so the figure is not cleanly of one period. Nothing else opened yields a group-scale count: emcoholding.com and the ILCS subsoil-companies entry on Inversiones Los Pinares were both refused with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (lapsed fetch permission, the requests were never put to the user), and the UN special-procedures letter of 3 November 2021 gives case detail (one mining licence, 217 hectares inside the Carlos Escaleras national park), not company scale. The E&N figures stay recorded here if the owner wants them, labelled for what they are.

ly-yong-phat.total: He signed the concession agreement of 2 August 2006 for Koh Kong Plantation Co., one of two adjacent Koh Kong concessions granted that day that together formed a 20,000-hectare industrial sugar plantation; according to the Ministry of Commerce he completely divested his shares in the Koh Kong sugar plantations in December 2009 (Licadho, 21 August 2014).

sources_add.title: Response to Phnom Penh Sugar Company's Allegations Against Equitable Cambodia Executive Director Eang Vuthy (21 August 2014)
sources_add.publisher: Licadho (Cambodian League for the Promotion and Defense of Human Rights)

ly-yong-phat.note: Corrected: the roughly 40,000-hectare sum is cut, and with it the three Oddar Meanchey concessions. I opened both sources. The Koh Kong half holds up and is now the whole sentence: Licadho states that the Koh Kong Plantation Co. concession agreement is dated 2 August 2006 and was signed by Ly Yong Phat, who is named as the company's Director, that an adjacent concession went to Koh Kong Sugar Co. the same day, that the two together form a '20,000 hectare industrial sugar plantation', and that per the Ministry of Commerce he 'completely divested his shares in the Koh Kong sugar plantations in December 2009'. That rests on a document he put his own name to, in one year, from one source, with the end of his interest stated - so the figure is in his name and dated. The Oddar Meanchey 19,736 hectares cannot be put in his name. The ActionAid Cambodia and Oxfam report (May 2015) confirms the hectares - Angkor Sugar 6,523, Cambodia Cane and Sugar Valley 6,595, Tonle Sugar Cane 6,618, total 19,736, contracts signed 24 January 2008 - but its link to him is 'some reported affiliations between the three companies with CPP Senator Ly Yong Phat and his company LYP Group', resting on a shared head-office address on the Ministry of Commerce website and a commune councillor saying the concessionaires 'are under the control of Yong Phat'. Licadho is blunter still: the three companies were 'believed to be owned wholly or partly by Mitr Phol', and of Ly Yong Phat it says only that he 'is clearly affiliated in some way with these businesses'. A reported affiliation of unstated kind, against a named other owner, is not a holding or a post, and the brief asks what the person oversaw. The sum was also unsound on its own terms: it added hectares established by a signed concession agreement to hectares linked only by inference, across concessions granted two years apart, to produce a single round figure whose two halves carry different standards of proof - a reader cannot see from '40,000 hectares' that half of it is contested. The ActionAid report is dropped from sources_add because no figure now rests on it; it remains worth citing in the map's case text for the Oddar Meanchey displacement itself. Also noted and left out, as the writer had it: the undated Phnom Penh Post list of six concessions totalling about 61,000 hectares, and the US Treasury designation of 12 September 2024, which calls L.Y.P. Group his conglomerate and names four hotels and resorts but gives no group-scale count.
